title: To-do app for the command line
prompt:
Build a command-line to-do app in Python as a package folder todo/ with todo/__init__.py, todo/storage.py and todo/__main__.py, so it runs as `python -m todo`.
Tasks are saved as JSON in the file named by the environment variable TODO_FILE (default: todo.json in the current folder). The file holds {"next_id": 1, "tasks": []}; each task is {"id": int, "text": str, "done": bool}. Ids start at 1 and are never reused, even after a task is removed.
In todo/storage.py write load(path) (a missing file gives {"next_id": 1, "tasks": []}) and save(path, data).
Commands and exactly what they print:
- python -m todo add "Buy milk"  ->  Added 1: Buy milk
- python -m todo list  ->  one line per task: `1 [ ] Buy milk`, or `1 [x] Buy milk` when done; `No tasks` when there are none
- python -m todo list --pending  ->  only the tasks not done (same format; `No tasks` if none)
- python -m todo done 1  ->  Done 1: Buy milk
- python -m todo remove 1  ->  Removed 1: Buy milk
- done or remove with an id that does not exist prints `No task 7` to stderr and exits with code 1.
Write unit tests too.
